achievements.mhDescription: Generated from your real activity — Steam hours played (exact, read from your own Steam), and Retro Mode sessions measured by MegaHUB itself. The rest of the launchers (Epic/GOG/Battle.net/etc.) only count as "launched" for streaks, since they run outside of what MegaHUB can reach.
achievements.raConnectIntro: Connect your RetroAchievements account to see your achievements profile here — games, progress and history, just like Steam or Xbox.
achievements.raKeyNote: Get your free key from your Control Panel → It's not your password — it's a read-only token. MegaHUB never sees or stores your password.
achievements.consolasDescription: Achievements and trophies read directly from the local files each emulator generates — no account or network needed. RPCS3 still doesn't reliably expose which trophies you've already unlocked (undocumented proprietary format); for now the full catalog for each game is shown.

onboarding.step1Copy: We already scanned your PC: Steam, Battle.net, Rockstar, Ubisoft and EA are detected automatically. If you also use GOG or Epic Games, connect them here to add them to your library.
onboarding.step2Copy: 10 skins with their own shape and identity, not just color — you can change it anytime from Settings → Appearance.
onboarding.step3Copy: MegaHUB also emulates consoles, from the Atari 2600 to the Xbox 360 — it installs cores, sets up folders and matches your ROMs against a public catalog. If you don't play retro, there's no need to touch anything here.

settings.title: Settings
settings.launchersIntro: Turn platforms on or off to control what shows up in your library. The ones marked "coming soon" are already on the roadmap, but MegaHUB can't read them yet.
settings.romsFolderIntro: Root folder where MegaHUB creates emulators/ and roms/ for consoles that don't have their own manually set location. By default it's your Documents folder (always writable, no matter where MegaHUB was installed).
settings.skinsIntro: Install community menu themes (XMB/RGUI) directly into your RetroArch, without having to copy folders by hand. The original is backed up before being replaced.
settings.guideSummary: Reference guide: recommended emulator per console
settings.guideIntro: The most popular/functional one per console up through PS3/Xbox 360. Most run as a RetroArch core; the heavier ones (Dolphin, PCSX2, RPCS3, Xenia…) perform better as a standalone program.
settings.tgdbGuideIntro: Covers already work without a key (libretro-thumbnails). For genre, developer, description and date you need your own free TheGamesDB key:
settings.tgdbCreateAccountLink: Create an account and get the free key →
settings.appearanceIntro: Changes the color palette for all of MegaHUB — it applies instantly and is remembered between sessions. (Not to be confused with RetroArch's "Themes" in Retro Mode: that changes the emulator's menu, this changes MegaHUB.)
settings.widgetAutohideLabel: Auto-hide when docked to a screen edge
settings.widgetAutohideIntro: If you drag the widget to a screen edge, turning this on makes it collapse into a thin strip when you move the mouse away (like the Windows taskbar) and expand again when you hover over it. Turn it off if you'd rather it stay fixed, like a normal dock, never collapsing.
settings.backupIntro: Save your settings to a .json file and take it to another PC (USB, email, your own personal cloud — MegaHUB never uploads anything on its own). Includes: emulator/ROMs folders you set by hand, your SteamGridDB/TheGamesDB keys, your RetroAchievements account, your MegaHUB achievement progress and the games you hid. Does not include GOG/Epic sessions (you'll need to reconnect them on the new PC) or cover/metadata caches (those get fetched again on their own).
settings.ecosystemNote: DERIVA ecosystem: if you have DERIVA Companion installed, MegaHUB shares with it — only on your own PC, with no server or account — what you're currently playing and a summary of your achievements, so they show up in DERIVA's gaming mode and profile. Neither app needs the other to work.
settings.creditsIntro: MegaHUB doesn't reproduce any console or manufacturer's logos or trademarks — the catalog icons are generic hardware silhouettes, chosen specifically to avoid that.
settings.consoleIconsCredit: Project RetroArch / libretro (retroarch-assets), XMB menu theme "Monochrome", originally created by Kivutar.
settings.consoleIconsLicense: License: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) — recolored per console in compliance with the license (it allows modification with attribution).

romFormatNote.noInfo: Use whichever ROM format ${emulator} reads (check its documentation).
romFormatNote.zipOk: You can also leave the game compressed as .zip or .7z — it reads it the same way, no need to unzip it yourself.
romFormatNote.noZip: This system does NOT accept .zip/.rar here: it has to be the disc/ROM file as-is, uncompressed.

notes.naomi: Same as Arcade, the .zip is the native romset (MAME format) — not just any compressed game. Naomi needs "naomi.zip" (BIOS) and Atomiswave "awbios.zip" in the same folder for their games to boot.
notes.xbox: Heads up: it has to be "xiso" format (converted with xdvdfs/Qwix), not a regular disc ISO.
notes.ps2: Avoid .bin/.cue: PCSX2 doesn't read them directly, convert them first.
notes.ps3: The .iso is the full disc image; the PS3_GAME/... folder is the disc as-is, unpackaged; .pkg is for digital copies. RPCS3 also needs the official PS3 firmware (PS3UPDAT.PUP) installed inside the emulator itself — it's set up there, not by placing a file in this folder.
notes.arcade: Unlike the rest, the .zip here is NOT optional: it is the romset's native format (the same one MAME/FBNeo use), with the exact internal files each game expects — it's not just "a compressed game".
notes.neogeo: Same as Arcade, the .zip is the native romset (MAME/FBNeo format). Many Neo Geo games also need the "neogeo.zip" romset (the system's shared BIOS) in the same folder.

leeme.emulator:
Folder for ${emulator} (${consoleName}).

MegaHUB does NOT include or download BIOS files: they're copyrighted and illegal
to redistribute. If this console needs a BIOS, get it yourself and place it
here however the emulator asks for it once installed.

Use the "Download emulator" link in MegaHUB to get the official installer
and unzip/install it into this folder if the emulator is portable.
leeme.roms:
Place your own backup copies of ${consoleName} games here.

${formatNote}

For MegaHUB to recognize the right cover, name the file EXACTLY like the
catalog title — the extension doesn't matter, only the name before it
(upper/lowercase doesn't matter either). Examples:
  "Super Mario Bros."  ✔ gets recognized (with any of the formats above)
  "backup copy" ✘ cannot be identified
